content:
maria: Heads up — during the 12:30 spike today p99 for /generate jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s after a scale-up. Noticed kernel fallback logs and lots of KV misses. link: https://perf.internal/redwood/runs/1781001122 :eyes:
jon: ugh. did the autoscaler add new workers or a different node-type?
sophie: autoscaler added 4 nodes (g5x2 -> g5x4 mix) at 12:29:47 according to deploy-bot. deploy-bot: added capacity group "burst-02" (4 instances).
maria: paste of the tail from runtime logs (truncated):
```
[12:29:52] request_id=abc123 kernel=fallback selected=quant_kv_v1 -> native_fp16
[12:29:52] request_id=abc123 kv_cache=miss shard=5
[12:29:52] microbatch_size=1 queue_wait=12ms exec=1.6s total=1.628s
[12:29:53] request_id=def456 kernel=optimal selected=quant_kv_v1 kv_cache=hit exec=120ms total=142ms
```
jon: interesting that microbatch_size is 1 for the slow requests — that suggests cold KV or missing batching. Did batching heuristics get reset after scale?
sam: we have heuristics that adjust max_microbatch by observed latency, but when nodes are new we fall back to conservative batch=1 until kernel warm metrics arrive. that's on purpose to avoid oversizing.
lee: right, but the issue is the combination: new node + cold KV + kernel fallback to slower path. Taken together creates p99 spikes.
sophie: perf-bot shows KV hit-rate dropped from 97% -> 22% for that shard during the window. perf-bot: KV hit summary: before=97.1% after=22.4%
maria: does anyone have a quick experiment we can run to validate which knob gives the biggest improvement: preheat KV vs force microbatch cap to 8 vs force kernel preferred?
\oncall: @jon @sophie can we run a canary with preheat + keep microbatch_max=8?
jon: I can spin up a dev cluster and replay the midday trace. Plan: 1) replay trace against new nodes with no preheat 2) replay with KV preheat script 3) replay with microbatch_max=8 4) replay with both.
sam: preheat script is basically a set of prefix requests that populate KV LRU. quick command: 
```
curl -X POST "https://runtime.internal/preheat" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","shards":[0..15],"prefixes_file":"/tmp/prefixes.txt"}'
```
lee: also add a kernel warm probe: small synthetic runs to ensure kernel selection profile is cached. e.g. `python tools/kernel_probe.py --model redwood-v1 --seq 512 --reps 20`
sophie: results from initial dev replay (no preheat): p50=110ms p95=380ms p99=1.7s kv_hit=21% microbatch_median=1 kernel_fallback_rate=34%
jon: with KV preheat only: p50=118ms p95=210ms p99=420ms kv_hit=92% microbatch_median=4 kernel_fallback_rate=6%
maria: wow, preheat alone drops p99 massively. That suggests KV staleness is the dominant factor for the spike, not autoscale latency alone.
sam: good find — preheat also increased batching because requests didn't get forced to microbatch=1 as often. caching & batching interact.
lee: I can PR an autoscaler hook that triggers a preheat job targeting the new instances' shards as soon as they pass healthchecks. small patch: autoscaler -> post-scale hook -> schedule preheat.
sophie: one caution: preheat traffic costs tokens — need to estimate cost. For 16 shards * 100 prefixes ~= 1600 requests per scale event. still cheaper than p99 hurting customers.
jon: alternative: keep a short-lived 'bootstrap' pooling tier: keep a minimal warm instance per shard during low load so new nodes get less cold. But that's more infra-y.
maria: actionable: 1) implement preheat post-scale hook (lee) 2) tighten microbatch heuristic so we only force microbatch=1 when kernel fallback observed and KV miss rate > 50% (sam) 3) add metric to dashboards: kv_hit_by_shard and kernel_fallback_rate_by_node (sophie)
sam: I'll write the microbatch heuristic change and add unit tests.
lee: I'll open autoscaler PR with preheat hook and a small retry/backoff for preheat jobs. PR link (draft): https://git.internal/redwood/autoscaler/pulls/482
sophie: adding the new panels to the runtime perf dashboard now.
maria: followups: run a production canary next Tuesday during low-traffic window, monitor p99 and cost delta. Also add a playbook entry to incident runbook about "scale-up KV cold start" with signal set.
jon: assign who will run the canary? @maria you want to own?
maria: I can coordinate but would like @sam to own microbatch change rollout.
sam: yep I'll be on-call for rollout.
maria: thanks all. :rocket:
deploy-bot: scheduled canary job for 2026-03-24T03:00Z per request.
